portabilityPatch.reason: cpu.CacheLinePad has size zero on WASM; retain a 64-byte minimum padding

metadata.goBuild: go build -trimpath -ldflags='-s -w'; default native optimization; no WASM engine
metadata.rustBuild: cargo build --locked --release; native opt-level=3, thin LTO, codegen-units=1, strip=true, panic=abort

methodology.sqlite: Native library calls in an already-open in-memory SQLite transaction. Includes SQL preparation, reads, stored JSON decoding, validation and evaluation. No outer request/response JSON serialization, WASM, IPC, network or transaction begin/commit costs. Native Go uses a typed Request; native Rust uses a serde_json::Value envelope.
methodology.json: Pre-encoded identical hydrated input bytes passed directly to each native Run function, then response decoding. Includes model/CEL validation, snapshot construction and evaluation. Excludes SQL and input encoding. Matches the scope of the earlier hydrated WASM invocation more closely than the structured native library mode.
methodology.upstream: Unmodified upstream commands.NewCheckCommand and graph.NewLocalChecker, bound through a new transaction-only RelationshipTupleReader over wasmfga's two-table schema. Accepts a native protobuf CheckRequest pre-decoded outside timing. Reads relevant edges directly; no complete-store hydration. Not the standalone HTTP/gRPC server or stock OpenFGA SQL backend. Same dispatch depth 25 and breadth 1 as the Go snapshot port. No tuple/decision cache.
methodology.cached: The separate upstream-cached variant prepares the immutable model and resolver once per workload/transaction outside timing; preparation is recorded. The other three SQLite variants reload/validate models per Check. This is an application configuration difference, not an isolated language comparison.
methodology.statistics: Five fresh processes per engine/mode by default, sequential execution, rotating engine order. Median of process medians and median of process p95 values; raw samples and range of medians retained. Small workloads: 500 warmups/5000 measured checks; 1000 tuples: 100/500; 10000 tuples: 10/50. Counts are multiplied by the recorded scale. Every decision verified outside its timed interval. No GC forcing, CPU pinning or profiler.
methodology.limitations: Rust remains experimental with known conformance gaps including a contextual-duplicate false allow. All measured workloads pass the native OpenFGA oracle; that does not establish general equivalence. Go snapshot hydration still uses quadratic upstream MemoryBackend.Write; direct upstream SQL avoids it. Go and Rust use different SQLite bindings/builds. One in-flight Check at a time; Go may dispatch graph branches using goroutines. One machine, no remote or durable-commit costs. Earlier WASM results were collected in a separate run; cross-run ratios are descriptive, not a simultaneous controlled comparison.

gate.scope: Ten shared valid Check workloads only. This is not unrestricted conformance; the Rust port retains the known CEL gaps and contextual-duplicate false allow documented in docs/conformance-audit.md.
